summary: Proxy idle-teardown leading to orphaned SSE fragments and missing terminal event
description: Issue summary: Customer sees intermittent truncated streamed responses and JSON parse failures when using SSE through their corporate reverse proxy. The client receives fragments (partial JSON objects) that never conclude with the terminal 'end' event. In many cases the final closing bracket and metadata are missing, causing the client's parser to throw and drop the response. Impact: End-user chat sessions sometimes render only partial paragraphs; escalated by Parcelly because this affects confirmation messages for shipments (~5-8% of streaming sessions during peak).
steps_to_reproduce: 1) Customer environment: browser client opens SSE to our /v1/stream endpoint via an on-prem reverse proxy (corporate appliance) that applies aggressive idle timeouts (60s) and HTTP/1.1 to HTTP/2 conversion.
2) Start a long streaming generation (~>500 tokens) targeting redwood-open-13B pinned on dedicated capacity.
3) Simulate idle by pausing client network (background tab or manual pause) for ~70s to trigger proxy idle teardown.

4) Resume network and let client reconnect (SSE reconnection logic kicks in). Observe client logs: parser errors and missing terminal 'event: end' chunk; server logs show trailing bytes sent prior to connection close.
5) Repro with curl from within their network: `curl -N -H 'Accept: text/event-stream' https://api.redwood.example/v1/stream -v` and watch for truncated last event after proxy RST during idle timeout.
logs: Excerpt from customer-provided client console: 'SSE parse error: Unexpected end of JSON input at position 243' — Upstream server logs (correlated) show 'connection half-closed: wrote tail bytes after FIN' and edge-proxy shows 'idle timeout: closed connection (RST)'. Packet-level capture (pcap) from customer shows server FIN then proxy RST while server still had buffered chunks to send.
investigation_notes: 2026-03-10 14:10 - Reproduced in staging with NGINX reverse proxy configured to idle_timeout 60s and proxy_buffering on. Observed race where backend wrote final streaming fragments while proxy was already closing on idle; proxy forwarded an RST to client and then the client's reconnection created a fresh session where resume logic attempted to stitch but missing terminal marker caused finalization to be skipped.

Hypothesis: The proxy idle teardown (RST) can occur *while* the serving-runtime flushes trailing chunks. Those trailing bytes end up in proxy buffers and may be dropped or delivered as a partial fragment on a new connection depending on how the proxy converts conn state (HTTP/1.1 <-> HTTP/2). Resume logic expects a clean end-event; seeing a stray mid-fragment or missing end leads to parser error and client drop.

Checked codepath: resume token/offset mapping in session-store marks streams terminal only on receipt of explicit end event. If bytes are lost at socket boundary, there is no fallback to 'force-terminate' based on connection close metadata. The edge currently does not synthesize a terminal event on socket RST from the proxy.
Observed that turning off proxy_buffering and increasing keepalive/idle timeout reduced rate of occurrences in staging to near zero.
SRE note: cloud provider LB also has an idle probe (120s). Customer appliance's tighter 60s window exposes the race more frequently than typical cloud LBs.
Severity assessment: customer-visible and user-facing UX regression; P1/Sev1 justified because Parcelly has high volume flows relying on guaranteed final output for confirmations.
root_cause: Interplay between aggressive proxy idle teardown (RST) and server-side streaming flush: partial trailing fragments are dropped or reattached incorrectly across connection handoffs, and server-side resume logic does not synthesize/force terminal events on abrupt socket teardown.
workarounds: Short-term for customer: increase proxy idle timeout to >= 180s OR disable aggressive proxy_buffering for SSE endpoints. If changer not possible, configure the client to treat parse errors as retriable and trigger a fresh non-resume request to fetch final summary (non-streaming fallback).
Client-side mitigation: add tolerant JSON reassembly logic that waits ~500ms for trailing bytes before failing; accept partial+retry flow for confirmation messages.

Server-side quick mitigation: enable explicit chunk delimiter payloads ('__STREAM_END__') emitted on connection close path (temporary flag rollout) so that some proxies pass through an identifiable closing marker.
resolution: In progress - mitigation applied and customer confirmed reduced failure rate. Engineering epic created to harden resume logic and add a server-side guard that force-closes sessions with a synthesized terminal event when upstream socket RST is detected.
resolution_notes: 2026-03-11: Support applied temporary mitigation guidance to Parcelly. They increased proxy idle timeout to 300s; incidents dropped in production from ~6% to ~0.3%.

2026-03-12: Engineering Triage -> created GH issue gh:redwood-inference/serving-runtime#2231 to implement: (A) detect upstream connection RST and mark stream terminal; (B) best-effort retry to deliver missing terminal marker to client on resume or synthesize end event in session-store.

2026-03-13: Staging test with synthesized terminal event logic shows deterministic recoveries for previously failing repros. Plan: release patch to edge+serving-runtime in next canary (target 2026-03-18) and monitor 48h before broader rollout.
Follow-ups: Update runbook Confluence:Runbooks/SSE-connection-handoff with proxy config recommendations and add an observability dashboard for 'sse-terminal-missing' metric.
